title: TAL appoints head of partnership for Aware Super
full_text:
TAL Australia has announced the appointment of Mary Gabriel to the position of head of partnership, Aware Super.
In her role, Gabriel will be responsible for leading TAL’s relationship with Aware Super and supporting the delivery of insurance outcomes for its members.
The two parties have had a relationship for many years as the core insurance provider for Aware Super members for death, TPD and income protection as well as those members previously with Telstra Super which merged with Aware earlier this year in a $235 billion deal.
Gabriel joins TAL with more than 25 years of experience from across the life insurance and financial sectors, with her most recent roles being head of corporate accounts at Angle Auto Finance and head of growth at Workzilla.
She also spent 12 years at MetLife Australia where she held multiple senior roles including senior client relationship manager, corporate markets, senior client manager, sales enablement and project manager and business development manager.
Her appointment is part of TAL’s ongoing investment in its partnerships capabilities and support for superannuation funds and their members, the life insurer said.
“Mary brings deep partnerships experience and strong industry knowledge to TAL,” Jenny Oliver, chief executive, group life and retirement, said.
“She has a strong understanding of the superannuation and insurance sectors and will play an important role in supporting our partnership with Aware Super and the members we collectively serve.”
Speaking on her appointment, Gabriel said she was excited to join TAL and was looking forward to maintaining its relationship with Aware Super.
“I’m looking forward to working with both teams to help superannuation members feel confident about their insurance protection and financial future,” she said via LinkedIn.
“With a history spanning more than 150 years, TAL has long been focused on protecting Australians when they need it most, helping people look after what matters most. I’m thrilled to be joining the team.”
This announcement comes hot on the heels of AMP North announcing its new TAL-underwritten insurance product, the platform being pitched as giving eligible clients a “simpler” way to access or transfer group insurance.
North said this process will be simplified through as few as three yes-or-no risk control questions.
“Advisers told us they wanted a simpler way to bring their clients’ super, investments and insurance together. North Protect gives them practical options to do that,” Edwina Maloney, AMP group executive, platforms, said of its launch.
“For clients with super and insurance spread across different funds, consolidation can be complicated by the need to retain appropriate protection. North Protect gives advisers another option to help simplify those arrangements.”
